topics.topic: Module ownership and enforcement boundaries for INV-11 prohibitions
questions: Which module owns and enforces each part of INV-11—holding no Portal credential, never calling the Portal, and returning no server path—given that `deliverer_api` can control answers but cannot control other modules' credentials or outbound clients?

topics.topic: Scope of the service network-access prohibition
questions: Does the prohibition cover direct HTTP access to the loopback listener by another process on the VPS, or only access originating outside the VPS?

quotes:
The deliverer runs on the VPS that holds the Client Portal, where it sees the Syncthing folders and
the Portal store. The kernel reaches it over HTTPS through the Portal's own front, under a route of
its own, with the deliverer's own credential; the deliverer is not reachable from the network in
any other way. How the route and the credential are installed belongs to the deployment.
The owner's kernel runs on the owner's PC and reaches the VPS only over HTTPS.

The service listens on the loopback interface, the address of the imported `BIND_HOST` constant. A reverse proxy on the same host terminates
   HTTPS for any caller from outside. The service reads no forwarded header.
There is one principal: the calling flow of the owner. It may act on every confirmed connection.
judgement.why: The texts do not admit the draft witness's second VPS process as a caller or say that it may possess the credential, while the only named principal runs on the owner's PC and reaches the VPS only over HTTPS, so no witness for differing direct-loopback behavior can be built.
